inputs.text: This case with Ms Mary Ngechi Ngethe exposes how elites in powerful institutional roles routinely siphon public resources that should support the most marginalized and working-class communities. The court recovered the Ksh.283 million from her after she chaired the Technical Evaluation Committee and drove the irregular purchase of unsuitable land for a cemetery. These procurement failures aren't random errors but predictable results of entrenched structural inequalities that let the connected few advance their interests while denying ordinary people basic dignity, including access to proper burial sites. Real change requires confronting and dismantling the systemic protections that shield these elites so our institutions stop perpetuating harm and exclusion and start serving the vulnerable instead.
